intro.title: Hello, I'm Qiang Wang
intro.desc: I am a 2027 master’s candidate in Transportation Engineering at Wuhan University of Technology, focusing on autonomous driving planning and control. At Jiwei and Neolix, I worked across production issue diagnosis, simulation, obstacle avoidance, speed planning, and joint path-speed optimization. I use C++, ROS, and optimization-based control, and helped test 15 real-vehicle scenarios with the national-champion OnSite team.

item0.title: Neolix · PNC Algorithm Intern
item0.desc: Built planning and control for autonomous delivery vehicles in tight turns, multi-obstacle detours, and uncertain oncoming-traffic conflicts. Designed XY-sliced DAG driving corridors, pruning dead ends with BFS, vehicle reachability, and reverse checks. Developed a two-branch CMPC/OSQP speed planner, then extended Path iLQR to optimize path and speed together with lateral-acceleration and jerk constraints for safer, smoother driving.
item0.imageAlt: Neolix internship vehicle photo and planning algorithm diagrams

item1.title: Jiwei · PNC Algorithm Intern
item1.desc: Traced production issues through logs, code, and simulation, helping close 50+ cases with an average turnaround of about two days. To prevent unnecessary detours around queued traffic, combined vehicle state, brake-light timing, behavior history, and temporal hysteresis into stable follow-and-stop decisions. Reworked direction-aware TCD search and corridor boundaries around fast oncoming vehicles to reduce lane-crossing and collision risk.

item0.title: OnSite Autonomous Driving Competition · National Champion
item0.desc: As a member of the national-champion team, helped complete closed-course vehicle runs across 15 scenario types, including pedestrian crossings, following, curves, merges, and roundabouts. Owned longitudinal decisions that combine traffic lights, pedestrians, and road geometry into safe speed limits using IDM and TTC. Developed and tuned CILQR local planning, supported NMPC tracking tests, and used RViz to expose road boundaries, predicted obstacle paths, and control states for faster debugging.

item0.title: Autonomous Control for SPMT Vehicles
item0.desc: For low-speed, heavy-duty SPMT path tracking and rear docking, integrated and calibrated inertial navigation, converted WGS84 positions to UTM, and compensated antenna, front, rear-axle, and docking points. Generated reference paths with Spline2D and computed lateral and heading errors. Tuned Pure Pursuit steering and PID speed control, then reviewed vehicle data from forward, reverse, figure-eight, double-lane-change, and docking tests to improve tracking and stopping accuracy.
